shots.purpose: Introduce Fuzzby for the first time -- zooming in and out erratically while clipping flowers and singing his own chaos-chant, until a botched somersault spirals into a genuinely spectacular tumbling pass he never intended, and he claims full, undeserved credit for it.
shots.performanceAssignment: Fuzzby's flight is one big outward loop around the meadow, no fixed heading within it -- he darts, overshoots, corrects, all while singing. Each flower clip is a real physical event: his body catches the stem, pollen bursts, he barely registers it and keeps singing. The somersault attempt is a genuine loss of control, not a stunt he's aiming for -- his own momentum carries him from one flower-bounce into the next, faster each time and visibly curving him back around his own loop, until one much bigger, more violent bounce than any before it launches him into the air and his tumbling body, entirely out of his own control, executes the double backflip and triple twist. He crash-lands hard, right back at the exact spot he started from, upright by pure luck -- a real, forceful impact, not a gentle touchdown: stems snap, a genuinely large pollen cloud bursts outward, his body compresses hard on contact before rebounding. His own landing surprises him as much as it would surprise anyone watching. The beat between confusion and pride is the whole joke: he genuinely doesn't know what just happened, and then decides he meant it all along.
shots.camera: The camera launches with Fuzzby as he peels away from Zenny's flower in one continuous, wide swooping loop around the whole meadow, losing and re-finding him through stems and pollen as he goes; it stays with his loop and does not cut back to Zenny until his own momentum carries him back around to exactly where he started.

shots.cutInMotivation: Cutting out here is stronger than holding on Fuzzby's pose because the next beat needs a hard reset into his very next overreach -- lingering would over-reward a joke that already landed.

Mid-song, still out on his loop, he attempts a showy somersault -- it goes wrong instantly, ricocheting him into an accelerating chain of involuntary bounces off flower after flower, faster and more out of control with each impact, his own momentum now visibly curving him back around toward where he started.

One violent bounce -- much bigger than any before it -- flings him into a genuine, unintentional double backflip with three full twists, and he crash-lands hard right back at Zenny's own flower, upright by pure luck: a real, forceful impact that snaps stems and sends a huge pollen cloud exploding outward around him. He processes his own dumb luck with a beat of dazed confusion, then pride visibly settles over his face as he throws himself into a triumphant pose -- Zenny right there again, exactly where he left her.

'Nailed it.' must land by roughly the 11-second mark of this 15-second shot -- deliver it EARLY, not at the last possible moment.
